why: You never need the exact route, only the farthest index you can reach so far. Sweep left to right and extend that reach with i + nums[i]; if you ever stand past the reach, you are stuck at a zero.
hints: Instead of trying routes, ask: from the indices reachable so far, how far can I get?
Keep one number, reach = the farthest index reachable. Every index up to reach is reachable, so each one can push reach to i + nums[i].
One pass: if i > reach return false, else reach = max(reach, i + nums[i]). Return true at the end. O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: A single element [0] is already at the end: true.
A zero is only a trap if reach cannot get past it, as in [3,2,1,0,4].
You can stop early once reach >= n - 1.
